children: Auto stocks are in focus as brokerage firm Ambit Capital expects steady demand and comfortable margins to drive re-rating for the sector.

In its latest note on Monday, November 23, Ambit Capital said that original equipment makers (OEMs) have healthy order books and low channel inventory. The average selling price growth in the second quarter was better than expected across most OEMs, it said.

The spot commodity basket is down between 6% - 8% compared to the second quarter levels for passenger vehicles and two-wheelers. Lower commodities, price hikes and operating leverage will drive margin recovery, it added.
Ambit Capital said the earnings downgrade cycle is largely behind the passenger vehicle OEMs.
The brokerage has raised its volume estimates by 1%-3% across segments. It also raised its earnings per share (EPS) estimates by 2%-5% for two-wheeler OEMs, and by 6%-10% for passenger vehicle OEMs.
Ambit Capital's top "buys" are Hyundai Motor India, Eicher Motors and Mahindra and Mahindra (M&M).

For Hyundai Motor India, Ambit has raised its price target to ₹2,512 from ₹2,252 earlier. Its price target on Eicher Motors has also been revised higher to ₹9,000 from ₹8,434 earlier. Mahindra & Mahindra's share price target has also been raised to ₹3,900 from ₹3,237 earlier.
Meanwhile it has "sell" calls on Bajaj Auto, Hero MotoCorp India and Ashok Leyland.

For its bearish calls, Ambit marginally revised its price target on Bajaj Auto higher to ₹9,300 from ₹9,268 earlier, for Hero MotoCorp to ₹5,000 from ₹4,640, and for Ashok Leyland to ₹150 from ₹141 earlier.

Shares of Hyundai Motor India ended the previous session 0.2% lower at ₹2,215 apiece. The stock has gained 19.7% in the past month but is down 4.2% this year, so far.
Eicher Motors shares ended the previous session 0.7% up at ₹8,113 apiece. The stock has gained 14.8% in the past month.
M&M shares declined 1% in the previous session at ₹3,545 apiece. The stock has risen 23.9% in the past month but is down 5.7% this year, so far.
Bajaj Auto shares declined 0.5% to ₹10,765 apiece in the previous session. The stock has risen 6.9% in the past month and 12.6% this year, so far.
Hero MotoCorp shares declined 0.4% in the previous session to ₹5,536 apiece. The stock has risen 9.7% in the past month and is down 5.2% this year, so far.
Shares of Ashok Leyland ended the previous session 1.7% lower at ₹163.35 apiece. The stock has risen 12.7% in the past month and has declined 11.7% this year, so far.
